name: Hôtel du Couvent, a Luxury Collection Hotel
positioning: Former 17th-century Visitation convent in the pedestrian Old Town of Nice, with gardens, a Roman-inspired thermal circuit and suites that overlook the Mediterranean
best_for: Travelers who want a historic convent setting in Nice's Old Town
Guests looking for a garden pool and a Roman-inspired thermal circuit in the city
Couples and families wanting a suite with butler service

facts.text: The hotel occupies a 17th-century convent with a garden in Old Nice.
The hotel is located in the pedestrian Old Town of Nice.
Accommodation ranges from monastic-type cells to apartments with a sea view.
Each suite has a dedicated butler.
Some suites have a private garden with a dining table, or terraces and loggias overlooking the Cour des Orangers.
Some suites have large kitchens equipped with Lacanche ranges.
In the Roman Baths, bathers start in the warm tepidarium, move to the hot caldarium and finish with a plunge in the cool frigidarium.
The Movement Studio runs daily classes including functional training, breathwork, yoga, pilates, floor barre and animal flow.
The terraced gardens and cloisters overlook the city rooftops and the Mediterranean.
Plage du Galet on the Promenade des Anglais reserves sunbeds for hotel guests.
The hotel's own farm, Ferme Notre-Dame in Touët-sur-Var in the hills behind Nice, supplies its kitchens.
Bread is baked on-site in the room where the convent sisters once prepared their daily loaves.

highlights.text: The hotel is the former Visitation convent, set in the heart of the old town and overlooking the Mediterranean.

As a tribute to the Roman bath remains on the Cimiez hill, the hotel has a Roman-inspired thermal circuit, with treatments that draw on botanical actives from the garden and the old convent pharmacopoeia.
The garden pool looks out over the terracotta rooftops of Nice on one side and the Mediterranean on the other.
Suites are decorated with bespoke furniture, antiques, sculptures, paintings and rare books.
A resident herbalist offers guests personalized guidance, handcrafted remedies and teas made with herbs from the garden.

considerations.text: The hotel is in the pedestrian Old Town: drivers go to the Old Town entrance on rue Centrale, and the valet service can escort guests to the hotel if called before arrival.
Rooms are spread across the convent's three buildings, and interiors and views vary from room to room.
The children's programme runs during school holidays, for ages 4 to 10.
